points.description: The essay states a clear position (thesis) on the issue and maintains that position throughout rather than being vague or shifting.
The position is supported with developed reasoning and evidence, not merely asserted or listed.
The essay is coherently organised, with ideas progressing logically (e.g. introduction, developed body, conclusion).
Language is precise and errors are few and do not obstruct meaning.

rubric.notes: Award marks for each descriptor in proportion to how fully it is met, then judge the essay as a whole against the 1-6 band scale in the model answer. Full marks correspond to a 6 (clear, well-developed position, strong reasoning and evidence, well organised, precise language, almost no errors); mid marks to a 3-4 (position present but development thin or uneven, some lapses and noticeable errors); low marks to a 1-2 (no clear position, little development, errors that obstruct meaning). Equivalent wording and alternative organisational patterns are acceptable; do not require any particular essay structure.
